title: The Close Call
logline: In a village cricket match, an umpire has a fraction of a second to decide a dismissal that will end someone's innings, and the whole ground waits, in silence, for the gap between seeing and deciding to close.
human_question: How much room is really there between something happening and a person's ruling on what it was?

premise.story: A village or town cricket tournament, following an umpire, and the players and crowd around a close decision, through a match, focusing on the moments where a fast, high-stakes call must be made.
premise.place: A village or town cricket ground during a local tournament.
premise.experience: The viewer feels the pause after an appeal, a held breath, a raised or withheld finger, and comes to notice how short and how real that gap actually is.

concept_links.why: The source's second class of process for a great object ends right at the burst of full response, with no lingering afterward, because the object itself has already ceased [C044-P:L33; C044-M:L9]. An umpire's instant call, with nothing to revisit once made, mirrors this exactly.
The source's rule that decision cannot coexist with doubt in the same moment [C025-P:L69] is dramatized by the visible pause of an umpire before the decision arrives.
The source's grading of how vividly an object presents itself, size, light, nearness, explains why some appeals are obvious and some are agonisingly close.

what_camera_could_observe: The delivery, the contact, the appeal
The umpire's face and stillness in the pause before the decision
The finger raised, or not, and the reaction that follows
Players and crowd reacting to a close call
Post-match conversation about calls that could have gone either way
what_must_be_real: Real matches and real decisions; no re-enacted or staged appeals. The umpire's own account of how he makes close calls, in his own words.

possible_arc.opening: A tournament match begins; early overs pass without incident.
possible_arc.turn: A genuinely close appeal forces a real, high-stakes decision.
possible_arc.ending_open: The match ends as it actually does, with whatever consequence the call actually had.

position_hint: middle: a public, high-tension setting that gives the group a burst of communal drama between its quieter craft films.

requirements: An active local cricket tournament with a willing umpire and organisers
Fast, reliable camera coverage of play, including close-in shots on the umpire
Consent from players, umpires and organisers to film real matches and decisions

suggestions.name: A village or town cricket tournament
suggestions.why: Local cricket tournaments are widespread and would supply real, unstaged close decisions.
suggestions.season_notes: Cricket season and tournament calendars vary by region and school or club schedule.
suggestions.verify: A specific tournament, ground and willing umpire are unconfirmed.

risks: Sports-highlight editing could flatten the film into a reflexes showcase
Slow motion could misleadingly suggest the moment is something a person can consciously watch happen, which the source denies
Focusing only on drama could lose the umpire's own account of the work
drop_if: No tournament or umpire allows genuine, unscripted filming of real decisions
The matches available turn out too low-stakes to carry real tension
The umpire is unwilling to reflect on how close calls are actually made

connections.note: Both trace the line between an object that barely registers and one that draws a full, decisive response.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
